clue.text: When it's dry, stalk (as one hears), making strides

indicators.note: what one hears is the spoken sound of a word, not its spelling

blocks.note: a kex is a dry, hollow plant stalk, such as hemlock's

explanation.surface: A hunter stalks briskly through dry grass, covering ground in long strides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strides' looks like a verb about walking, but it is British slang for trousers, and so is KEKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a pair of trousers.

clue.text: King's lad, up, on piano for a caper?

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: K is the abbreviation for king
son, read upwards
p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A royal boy climbs onto the piano for a bit of a lark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' suggests a prank, but a caper is a pickled flower bud.
explanation.definitionFit: A knosp is a bud or knob, so it names what a caper is, the bud of the caper bush.

clue.text: Soft inside, reheat a chopped groundnut

indicators.note: chopped means cut up into pieces, so these letters are rearranged
inside places the letter within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: the seven letters of the words, rearranged
p is the musical marking for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A recipe note: reheat a chopped peanut until soft inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The earth-pea is a pea-like plant whose pods ripen underground, a kind of groundnut.

clue.text: Caribbean music, unspecified, includes king in reggae dances

indicators.note: includes means holding something within, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: ska is a Jamaican music style
n.s. is the abbreviation for not specified
K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A note on Caribbean music: some unnamed style features a king of reggae dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unspecified' is a plain adjective in the surface, but it gives n.s., the abbreviation for not specified, which then holds the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A skank is a rhythmic dance performed to reggae music.

clue.text: Father's condition? Hopes dashed when opening spleen

indicators.note: hopes that are dashed are smashed to pieces, so the word is broken up and its letters rearranged
opening something lets another thing in, so the first word goes inside the second

blocks.note: the five letters of the word, rearranged
'the pip' is a fit of bad temper or spleen

explanation.surface: A father, his hopes dashed, finally vents his spleen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Holy Father is the Pope, so 'Father's condition' is the office or state of being Pope; the question mark flags that capital-F reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeship is the dignity or office held by the Pope, whom Catholics call the Holy Father.

clue.text: Ice cone delivered by GPO?

indicators.note: delivered is read as set loose, freeing the letters to fall into a new order

blocks.note: post that has been delivered is in
the General Post Office, taken as letters

explanation.surface: A frozen treat arrives by post from the General Post Office.
explanation.walkthrough: The GPO was Britain's General Post Office; the question mark flags that the parse is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A pingo is a conical mound of earth with a core of ice, found in permafrost regions.

clue.text: She'll play lead character of plenty in Norma, grabbing notice? (10, two words)

definitions.text: She'll play lead character of plenty in Norma, grabbing notice?

indicators.note: the lead character of a word is the one at its head, its first letter
play suggests loose movement, so these letters are free to move into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written
taken as written
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A diva who will sing the title role in Bellini's Norma, attracting plenty of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: Norma is a Bellini opera whose title role is a great soprano part.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is the leading female singer in an opera company, the one who takes the lead role.

clue.text: Cheers going up on Sabbath for old-style engagements

indicators.note: in a down light, going up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: roots, as in roots for a team, read upwards
S is an abbreviation for Sabbath

explanation.surface: Toasts rise on Sunday in honour of old-fashioned betrothals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagements' suggests betrothals, but here they are fights; 'cheers' is a verb, as in roots for.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoor is the Scots form of stour, an old word for a battle, conflict or tumult.

clue.text: Extremely busy A-road that I worked round (8, three words)

indicators.note: worked round means kneaded and reshaped, so these letters change their order

blocks.note: A, then RD, the abbreviation for road
taken as written

explanation.surface: A main road has been so heavily dug up that it is choked with traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-road is a British main road; here only the A and the abbreviation RD are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard at it is an idiom for working flat out, fully occupied with a task.

clue.text: Sexual activity? Then check prurience

blocks.note: it is a coy word for sex
ch. is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Someone asks about sex, then tells himself to rein in his lust.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch can mean a restless, lustful craving, the same sense as prurience.

clue.text: Is sleep disturbed? This should keep child warm

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown out of its settled state, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all seven letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent wonders if a child's sleep is broken, and what would keep the little one warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelisse is a long cloak or coat, in one sense a child's outdoor garment worn for warmth.

clue.text: Watch a queen being placed between knight and king

indicators.note: being placed between tells us to set the middle pieces side by side in the gap between the two chess pieces

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
taken as written
R, for regina, is a queen
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess player watches as a queen is slotted in between knight and king.
explanation.definitionFit: Nark, besides meaning a police informer, can mean to spy on or keep watch, as Chambers records.

clue.text: What can 10 mean? I v-value bagging it

indicators.note: bagging something puts it in a bag, so the stammered word holds the short word inside

blocks.note: taken as written
value is rate, and the stutter on its first letter carries over: r-rate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a cross-reference, followed by someone stammering over a value.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer is part of the wordplay: whatever word replaces 'value' must keep its doubled first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: NARK (10 across) also means to annoy or vex, which is what irritate means.

clue.text: Fine material, newspaper's hallmark?

blocks.note: an organ is a newspaper or journal that speaks for a group
a die is the stamp that strikes a mark into metal, as a hallmark is struck

explanation.surface: A newspaper's quality, its hallmark, is the fine material it prints.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: the die is the tool that makes a hallmark, so the organ's die is a newspaper's hallmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a very fine, stiffened transparent muslin, a light dress fabric.

clue.text: Pale green primate taken in half dead

indicators.note: taken in means drawn inside something else, so these pieces go within

blocks.note: eco- means environmentally green
a loris is a small primate
the first half of the word

explanation.surface: A sickly green monkey is captured in a half-dead state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale green' reads as one colour, but 'pale' is the definition, a verb, and 'green' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To decolorise is to remove colour, which is what pale means as a verb: to make or turn whiter.

clue.text: Unattached male at party round north pole

indicators.note: round says the first word goes around the next item, enclosing it

blocks.note: a stag is a man without a female partner, as at a stag party
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A single man at a party dances around a north pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At party' hints at a stag party and lies only in the surface; 'north pole' splits, north giving the letter and pole the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stang is a Scots and northern dialect word for a pole or wooden bar.

clue.text: Soul greeting enlightenment?

blocks.note: a bod is a person, as is a soul in 'not a soul'
a common greeting

explanation.surface: A spirit hails the arrival of spiritual light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soul' wants to be spiritual, but here it just means a person, colloquially a bod.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, bodhi is the state of supreme knowledge or awakening, the enlightenment the Buddha reached.

clue.text: Singer rarely seen today, wayward star restricted by censor

indicators.note: wayward means straying from the proper course, so the letters are rearranged
restricted by means hemmed in, so these letters sit inside

blocks.note: the four letters, rearranged
Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor

explanation.surface: A vanished singing star, kept off stage by the censor.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder is so famous as censor of Rome that he is often called Cato the Censor.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrato is a male singer castrated before puberty, a type unknown since the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Part of gem-cutter's kit in a drawer, among tins

indicators.note: among places these items in the midst of the cans, so they go inside

blocks.note: taken as written
dr. is the abbreviation for the drawer of a cheque
cans are tins

explanation.surface: A jeweller's tool lies in a drawer among a clutter of tins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' suggests a piece of furniture, but here it is the person who draws a cheque, abbreviated dr.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadrans is the instrument that holds a gem at a set angle while it is cut and polished.

clue.text: Outside allotment: a great amount is raised, about quarter consumed

indicators.note: consumed means eaten up, so one piece is swallowed inside another
in a down light, raised means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a ton is a great amount
qu. is the abbreviation for quarter
on means about, as in a talk on poetry

explanation.surface: A huge harvest grown beyond the garden plot, with a quarter eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allotment' suggests a British vegetable plot, but here it is a quota, a set share.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-quota describes goods or people not counted within a fixed quota, so outside the allotment.

clue.text: One whose work is irregular rarely tips Mossad off

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: all ten letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: An informant who seldom tips off Israeli intelligence keeps irregular hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Mossad is Israel's secret service; 'rarely' only warns that the answer is a rare word.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasmodist works in spasms, in fits and starts, so their output comes irregularly.

clue.text: Quarantine maybe on board ship creating lather?

definitions.note: the answer is a present-tense verb, 'makes lather'

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so the fruit goes between its letters

blocks.note: the quarantine or quarrender is an old variety of red apple
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Sailors in quarantine on a ship work up a lather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarantine' is not isolation here but a name for an apple variety, which Chambers lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapple is a Scots verb meaning to wash with soap and work up suds.

clue.text: Dish like blanquette de veau? (Cut leg in case going wrong)

indicators.note: going wrong means getting out of order, so the letters are scrambled
in places the first items inside the scrambled word

blocks.note: to lop is to cut off
pins is slang for legs
the four letters of the word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a veal dish fails when the leg is cut up wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Blanquette de veau is a French veal stew; the question mark marks the answer as one example of a veal dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaloppine are thin escalopes of veal, so like blanquette de veau it is a dish of veal.

clue.text: Wrong form of mincer

indicators.note: a form of something is a new shape of it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the six letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has a faulty kitchen mincer.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimen is Latin for a crime or charge, used in legal phrases, so a wrong in the legal sense.

clue.text: Grass, one interrupting flower?

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the word goes inside

blocks.note: the pick of a group is its flower, its finest part
an means one

explanation.surface: An informer breaks into a garden bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like an informer and 'flower' like a bloom; the first is a plant, the second means the best.
explanation.definitionFit: Panick, also spelt panic, is a millet-like grass, of the genus Panicum.

clue.text: Ship's captain housing most of company aboard vessel

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is kept
housing means putting something inside, as a house holds its occupant

blocks.note: a troop is a company of soldiers or players
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A sea captain takes most of his company on board his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like the ship, but it is a pan; 'aboard' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives patroon as an old word for the captain or master of a ship, beside its Dutch-American landholder sense.

clue.text: Church proclamation from bishop for instance, including names

indicators.note: including means taking in, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
as means for instance
n. is name, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A bishop issues a church notice which, for instance, lists names.
explanation.definitionFit: Banns are the announcement in church of an intended marriage, read so objections can be raised.

clue.text: The old get pie-eyed, shortly about to throw up

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut down to its first letter
in a down light, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to toss is to throw
the word cut short to its initial

explanation.surface: Old folk get drunk, and before long are sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks an archaic word; 'throw up' looks like vomiting but splits into throw plus the reversal sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Assot is an obsolete Spenserian verb meaning to besot, to make or become infatuated and befuddled.

clue.text: Capital: rupees in fractions thereof mostly

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped
in places the money inside the following word

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for rupees
paise are hundredths of a rupee

explanation.surface: A note on money: the capital held in rupees and their small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, matching the rupees, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France.

clue.text: Sally sometimes showing off, escaping from fling

indicators.note: escaping from means getting out, so certain letters leave the longer word

blocks.note: flaunting is showing off
these letters are the ones that leave

explanation.surface: Sally is sometimes caught showing off, and escapes after a brief affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove F, L, I, N, G from the longer word and the middle is left. An Aunt Sally is a fairground target, and so anyone set up for criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Sally sometimes comes after Aunt, as in Aunt Sally, the British fairground figure pelted with sticks.

clue.text: End of stick in bottom should get elephant moving!

definitions.note: a description of the thing, not a synonym

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of the following word is used
in places the letter inside the following word

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
the anus is at the bottom, in the anatomical sense

explanation.surface: A mahout's advice: a stick end in the backside will make an elephant move.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a prod in the rear; the answer is the very tool doing the prodding.
explanation.definitionFit: An ankus is the hooked goad an Indian elephant driver uses to steer and urge on the animal.

clue.text: Bell maybe favoured in chambers? They're certainly not grand

indicators.note: in places the short word inside the plural noun

blocks.note: Bell was a maker of pianos, so Bell's product is one example
in favour, or in, means popular or favoured

explanation.surface: Someone called Bell, much favoured in legal chambers, is clearly not grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' sounds like snobbery, but it is the grand piano; the small upright kind is the pianino.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianino is a small upright piano, the opposite in size of a concert grand.

clue.text: Begins section in alimentary canal (8, two words)

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the long word for the gut

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for section
the enteron is the alimentary canal

explanation.surface: Something starts a stretch of the digestive tract.
explanation.walkthrough: To enter on a task is to begin it.
explanation.definitionFit: Enters on is an older phrasal verb meaning starts or takes up, as in entering on a career.

clue.text: Administrative trainee accepted by company, one of two noted for sternness

definitions.text: one of two noted for sternness

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the trainee goes inside the company

blocks.note: AT is the civil-service abbreviation for an administrative trainee
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A civil-service trainee joins a firm and is known for being severe.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder and his great-grandson Cato the Younger were both famous Roman moralists.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Romans named Cato were proverbial for austere, rigid morals, so either one fits.

clue.text: Square smiters of the ball — tops

blocks.note: first meaning: batters who hit the ball hard, to tonk or stonk being slang for a hard hit
second meaning: beats or overwhelms, a slang verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tops' looks like a noun but is a verb here: Chambers gives stonker as slang for overwhelm or defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonkers can be heavy hitters of a ball and, as a verb, beats or gets the better of someone.

clue.text: Portion of whisky — a tumblerful — necessary in Rangoon

definitions.note: a cryptic sense: the money one needs in Burma

indicators.note: a portion is part of something, so the letters come from inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word, a whole word, and the start of another

explanation.surface: A traveller in Burma insists a glass of whisky is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangoon, now Yangon, was the capital of Burma (Myanmar); 'the necessary' is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The kyat is the currency unit of Myanmar, so it is the money one needs there.
